topic.symptom: A newly built PC does not boot.
topic.title: New Build Won't Boot? Check the CPU Power Cable

script: New build won't boot? Unplug it before opening the case. Find the CPU power socket by the CPU. Use the CPU cable, not a PCIe one. Push it all the way in. Plug it back in. Then try booting again.

storyboard.title: New Build Won't Boot? Check the CPU Power Cable
storyboard.narrationStyle: Calm, conversational, one check. The captions are burned into the cut; no voice generated.

beats.visualDirection: A finger presses the stylized PC's power button; the monitor beside it stays dark. No other symptom is shown.

beats.narration: Unplug it before opening the case.
beats.visualDirection: At the back of the power supply, the power cord comes out of the inlet.

beats.narration: Find the CPU power socket by the CPU.
beats.visualDirection: The glass side panel slides off; the camera closes on an empty 8-pin socket next to the CPU cooler, outlined amber, the cooler tagged CPU; marked EXAMPLE LAYOUT.

beats.narration: Use the CPU cable, not a PCIe one.
beats.visualDirection: Two cable ends face-on: the 4+4-pin end marked CPU gets a green tick; the 6+2-pin end marked PCIe gets a red cross.
beats.onScreenText: USE THE CPU CABLE → NOT THE PCIe ONE

beats.narration: Push it all the way in.
beats.visualDirection: Side view: the CPU plug lowers onto the socket, thumbs press it home, its latch hooks over the socket's tab; outlined green.
beats.onScreenText: PUSH IT ALL THE WAY IN → FULLY IN

beats.visualDirection: The camera pulls back from the filled socket; the panel slides back on; at the back, the cord goes back in.
The unlit PC beside the dark monitor, its power button pulsing amber. No one presses it; no boot is shown.

factualGuardrails: Never say: guaranteed cure for boot failures (It may not work; one check, never a guaranteed fix.)
Never say: always the sole culprit behind boot failures (A PC can fail to boot for many reasons; this is one check.)
Never say: identical header placement on all motherboards (Positions vary; the layout is labelled as an example and the manual decides.)
Never say: successfully boots straight into Windows afterwards (The cut ends before anyone presses the button; no boot is shown or promised.)
persistentDisclosures: Stylized example · not a fix for every PC

claims.proposition: unplug the power cable before working inside the PC
claims.basis: Crucial, "How to Install Memory in Your Desktop" (https://www.crucial.com/support/install-memory-desktop): "Shut down your system. Once your system has been powered off, unplug the power cable." Checked 2026-10-11 via search excerpts; the factual-takeaway gate re-reads it.

claims.proposition: a missing CPU power cable can stop a PC from booting
claims.basis: ASUS, "[Motherboard] Troubleshooting - No Power/No Boot/No Display (FAQ 1042632)" (https://www.asus.com/us/support/faq/1042632/): "Some motherboard may contain 8-pin EATX12V_1, 4-pin EATX12V_2 and 24-pin EATXPWR, we suggest to connect all three connectors to the power supply." Checked 2026-10-11 via search excerpts; the factual-takeaway gate re-reads it. Also: ASUS (H87M-PRO user manual, p. 1-24, as quoted on a forum), "H87M-PRO user manual" (https://www.hometheaterforum.com/community/threads/mobo-wont-power-8-pin-cpu-atx-12v.253413/): "Do not forget to connect the 4-pin/8-pin EATX 12V power plug. Otherwise, the system will not boot." Checked 2026-10-11 via search excerpts; the factual-takeaway gate re-reads it.

claims.proposition: the CPU power socket on the motherboard is next to the CPU
claims.basis: Corsair, "Do I Need to Plug in Both CPU Power Cables?" (https://www.corsair.com/us/en/explorer/diy-builder/power-supply-units/do-i-need-to-plug-in-both-cpu-power-cables/): "Just make sure the connector closest to the CPU socket is populated and you will be totally fine." Checked 2026-10-11 via search excerpts; the factual-takeaway gate re-reads it.

claims.proposition: a PCIe cable is not the CPU power cable and does not belong in that socket
claims.basis: Corsair, "Can I use a PCI-e cable in the 8-pin motherboard plug?" (https://www.corsair.com/ca/en/explorer/diy-builder/power-supply-units/can-i-use-a-pci-e-cable-in-the-8-pin-motherboard-plug/): "The connector is physically different, but also because the cables are wired differently and might damage your components." Checked 2026-10-11 via search excerpts; the factual-takeaway gate re-reads it.
